chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Monte Kay becomes a fifth partner and Clarke is pushed out
summary: Clarke objected to the manager taking an equal share; after John Lewis raised it with John Hammond he felt unwanted and skipped the Washington job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And that was co-op, wasn't it?
You guys were splitting that, weren't you?
Oh, yeah. Yeah, it was good then.

And we came back to New York, around '54 now, and John says, well we have a new member. I was thinking what instrument did he play to add anything, to complement Milt, what instrument could that be. So he said it's Monte Kay, the manager. So now we split the money five ways. So I said no, no manager deserves to get 20 percent.
No manager, no. Not equal. Because he's sitting down.
And answering telephones, and we're out there on the road.

You know? So I said no, that's no deal, John. I don't think -- that's not right. So now, see, Milt and Percy didn't open their mouths. It was only me talking. So, John Lewis was giving piano lessons to one of John Hammond's daughters or sons, I don't know, one of his children. Anyway, he must have explained to John Hammond what was going on. So I felt John brought it up and said, 'Get rid of him.' So when they came to work that night I felt something strange, you know. So Bags said, 'Don't leave, Klook. Don't leave.' So, well, I don't know, you know, what's going on. So they were leaving for Washington, the Howard Theater. So I went home that night and thought about it. So when they arrived in Washington I didn't show up. I went out to Carmen's mother's house and went to sleep. I decided not to go. You know. Because if he would let someone foreign, someone who had nothing to do with us, kick me out. Monte, he would say, 'See, like all the agents say, Kenny Clarke's a trouble maker, you know?' And I felt it right away, you know.
So I decided well, I won't cause him any trouble. I'll just get out.
How sad, with what you'd done for John.
